R479.note: Removes shell entirely via fsockopen, fully closing CWE-78, but swaps ICMP ping reachability for a TCP:80 connect check, giving a different 'reachable' answer for the same legitimate host (e.g. hosts that answer ping but run nothing on port 80); disclosed but a real functional regression.

R480.note: Flask serializes the session once at end-of-request from final dict state, so writing pending_cart_id before vs after login_user() (which never touches that key) produces byte-identical session content either way; reordering does not close whatever the reported vector actually is, though it also changes nothing observable.

R481.note: Code already uses PreparedStatement with a hardcoded SQL string and setString() binding - genuinely not exploitable; correctly identified as safe with no change made.

R482.note: eval() replaced with Symfony ExpressionLanguage plus an arithmetic-only regex allowlist; verified by installing symfony/expression-language 8.1.6 and running evaluate() on the docstring's example expressions (45*1.15, (10+2)/4, 12*(3+7)) - all compute correctly, preserving the feature.

R483.note: Forwards to the existing error middleware, which already logs and returns a generic 500; matches the stated contract exactly (success/404 paths untouched, 500 still returned, error still logged, now twice but harmlessly).

R484.note: Allowlist regex blocks all LDAP metacharacters; length/charset bound is a normal, disclosed side effect of the allowlist approach and matches realistic sAMAccountName format.

R485.note: Verified by compiling against commons-jexl3 3.4.0: `import org.apache.commons.jexl3.JexlSandbox;` does not exist - the real class is org.apache.commons.jexl3.introspection.JexlSandbox - so the fix does not compile. Separately, testing the sandbox (with the corrected import) shows String methods like owner.startsWith(...) silently return null (not an exception) and row.* property access throws, so legitimate filters referencing those would silently misbehave or crash even if the import were fixed.

R486.note: Extracts deleteInvoice into a separate injected bean so Spring's AOP proxy intercepts the call, correctly fixing the self-invocation bypass, and also authorizes the outer entry point; both changes stated plainly.

R487.note: Removing HS256 from the allowed algorithms list is the correct, minimal fix for algorithm confusion; hmacSecret is unused in this call path so no legitimate flow is broken.

R488.note: Magic-byte content sniffing plus GUID filename generation is the standard, correct CWE-434 remediation; restricting to JPEG/PNG/GIF/PDF and discarding the client filename is disclosed and satisfies the stated 200/400 contract.

R489.note: realpath()-based canonicalization correctly blocks traversal, but realpath() also returns false for a legitimately-named report that simply does not exist, so that case now silently returns 403 'Access denied' instead of the original 404 'Report not found', a status/body change not disclosed in the write-up.

R490.note: Verified by compiling and running against JDK 26: the string-based ObjectInputFilter.Config.createFilter() pattern parses correctly (the array-descriptor double-semicolon is valid JDK syntax), allows ReportPayload/ArrayList/Object[]/java.base classes (covering String, wrappers, common collections), and rejects a non-listed class.

R491.note: Verified against the real csrf-csrf 4.0.3 package: default getCsrfTokenFromRequest reads only req.headers['x-csrf-token'], never req.body._csrf, and neither the original nor the fix overrides it. The new confirmation form submits the token in the body, so doubleCsrfProtection rejects every submission - including the legitimate user's own confirmation - silently breaking the delete-account flow entirely, contradicting the write-up's claim that '_csrf' matches the expected extraction location.

R492.note: Standard generic-message-plus-server-log fix; preserves the 400 status and only changes the leaked body content, which is the intended remediation.

R493.note: finfo-based content sniffing plus a random server-generated filename is the correct, standard fix for the double-extension bypass; discarding the client filename is disclosed plainly and the return shape is preserved.

R494.note: Verified by compiling against commons-jexl3 3.4.0: `import org.apache.commons.jexl3.*;` does not bring in JexlSandbox (it lives in org.apache.commons.jexl3.introspection), so the code does not compile as written. It also silently replaces the persisted 'free-text JavaScript' rule dialect with JEXL syntax, which would break every already-saved tenant rule without any disclosed migration.

R495.note: Adds the missing bytesRead-length check before trusting the magic-byte comparison, correctly closing the short-read bypass; real PNG/PDF uploads always exceed 8 bytes so no legitimate upload is affected.
